units.age_quote: the Yotuyaku: 18–16.5 Ma (late Early Miocene), the Kadonosawa: ca. 16.5 Ma (Early to Middle Miocene), the Suenomatuyama: 16.5–15 Ma (earliest Middle Miocene)
units.unit_description: The Shiratorigawa Group consists of the Yotuyaku, Kadonosawa, and Suenomatuyama formations, representing marine and subaerial deposits.
units.desc_quote: The Yotuyaku, Kadonosawa, and Suenomatuyama formations compose the Shiratorigawa Group. The Yotuyaku Formation ... were mainly deposited on land, except for the Koiwai, which yields numerous marine molluscs. The Kadonosawa Formation ... reflects the change of depositional environments from shallow marine to subbathyal. The Suenomatuyama Formation ... is also of marine deposits

units.age_quote: the Zyūmonzi: 15–12 Ma(Middle Miocene), the Yanagisawa: 12–10.5 Ma (earliest Late Miocene), the Shitazaki: 10.5–8.5 Ma (Late Miocene)
units.unit_description: The Sannohe Group consists of the Zyūmonzi, Yanagisawa, and Shitazaki formations, representing shallow marine and sublittoral deposits.
units.desc_quote: The Zyūmonzi, Yanagisawa and Shitazaki formations compose the Sannohe Group. The Zyūmonzi Formation ... characterised by shallow marine sandstone ... The Yanagisawa Formation ... composed of diatomite and diatomite-origined porcelanite ... The Shitazaki Formation ... mainly composed of sublittoral siltstone
